correctness.rationale: For complex affine a+bz restricted to a proper closed arc, |a+e^{it}b|^2 is constant times (1+c cos(t-delta)), 0<=c<=1; the worst continuous-to-discrete quotient is attained at c=1 when it exceeds one. With endpoints span 4x and largest knot gap g>=4x/(m-1), the gap midpoint gives lower bound sec(g/4)>=sec(x/(m-1)); the antipodal phase to the endpoints gives at least sin(theta/2)/sin x. One increasing and one decreasing function cross at unique sin x=sin(theta/2)cos(x/(m-1)); the symmetric arithmetic inset grid achieves this bound by three phase regions, and equality forces centered endpoints and equal gaps. Scalar matrix coefficients <(A+zB)u,v> yield the same sharp constant at all Hilbert-space operator levels. The expansion gives theta^2/8 leading (m-1)^2(C-1), theta^2 tan(theta/2)/4 for inset, and budget from the two balanced inequalities. Independently sampled phase maxima on dense grids at (theta,m)=(0.7,3),(1.9,5),(3.05,8) and matched predicted secant constants within <1e-11. Not a global optimizer proof from finite grids: the analytic bounds/rigidity supply it.
